summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Fed to boost payment service fees
articles.description: The Federal Reserve is also instituting a new access fee that it says will create a more “streamlined experience” for its bank clients.

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard face possible trial
articles.description: If a court rejects final approval of a card-fee settlement over the networks’ swipe fees, the case will go to trial, a federal judge said.

articles.title: JPMorgan cards chief to depart
articles.description: Allison Beer, CEO of card and connected commerce, will leave JPMorgan for an external opportunity, according to a company memo.

articles.title: OpenAI wallet taps card networks
articles.description: The artificial intelligence company has created a digital wallet through which its ChatGPT agent can use Visa, Mastercard and American Express.

articles.title: Mastercard pilots AI travel purchases
articles.description: The card network is deploying its technology to validate consumers’ agentic transactions and hide their payment details in the process.

articles.title: POS competition lightens up
articles.description: Point-of-sale service providers are facing less intense competition in the market as venture-funded startups drop away, Shift4's CFO contended last week.

articles.title: Embedded finance in 2026: What merchants want (it’s not what you think)
articles.description: Business want simpler embedded finance. Discover what that means for your software strategy.

articles.title: Why “faster cash flow” sells embedded payments to US SMBs
articles.description: New research shows 65% of US SMBs use embedded payments, and what it takes to win the rest.
